programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing's Hutongs
programme.desc: The Hutongs in Beijing are considered the city's blood vessels, as these traditional alleyways make up the DNA of the capital for its rich history and culture.In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May zigzag their way through the Hutongs and the Forbidden City for a mouth-watering experience full of ancient and modern delicacies. Starring German designer Katrin, Russian artist Liuba and photographer Feng Yu from Beijing, our hosts are taking you along a journey that features fried noodles, dim sum, pancakes and co.!

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.3

Here, Tianran samples breakfast at a bustling local teahouse and experiences monastic life at the vast Tashilunpo Monastery. He then visits an agricultural park where tropical crops thrive against the odds of the alpine plateau, before discovering pulu — a traditional Tibetan textile now earning global acclaim.

programme.title: Foodwise: Beijing's Hutongs
programme.desc: The Hutongs in Beijing are considered the city's blood vessels, as these traditional alleyways make up the DNA of the capital for its rich history and culture.In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May zigzag their way through the Hutongs and the Forbidden City for a mouth-watering experience full of ancient and modern delicacies. programme.title: Suqian
programme.desc: Suqian is a small city in Jiangsu Province, which may not be so famous nowadays. In history, there was a famous figure here: Xiang Yu! Suqian is of great significance to our presenter Megan. Although she grew up in the United States, Suqian is her hometown. This time, let's follow the presenter to have a look at the local customs of her hometown that she always misses.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programme.desc: Kleber travels to Chenjiagou in central China, the birthplace of Chen-style Taiji Quan. Also known as tai chi, the martial art is iconic for its slow movements and purported health benefits, but Kleber quickly discovers it’s the real deal: From being thrown around by teenagers to learning about the martial art’s Yin-Yang philosophy, Kleber experiences for himself how this kungfu style allows small to defeat big, and soft to beat strong.

programme.title: The Elegance of Luoyang

programme.title: China Bound: Wuhan
programme.desc: Tianran He visits Wuhan, a megacity at the crossroads of central China. From experiencing its vibrant breakfast culture and iconic dishes like hot dry noodles to exploring the lakes and hills of the expansive East Lake, as well as historic districts that showcase a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, Tianran uncovers why Wuhan has been a pivotal city in Chinese history for centuries. Finally, he relives some of these moments through immersive theater performances set amongst historic buildings and aboard a steamship cruising the Yangtze River.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

programme.title: Foodwise：Qingdao

programme.title: Life as a Miao Embroidery Girl
programme.desc: In this episode, host Eva May travels to Maomaohe Village in Leishan County, Guizhou Province — a place renowned for its exquisite Miao embroidery. She spends a week immersing herself in the daily lives of local embroidery artisans, learning traditional Miao folk songs, and rising to the challenge of creating a piece of Miaoxiu embroidery with special cultural significance.

programme.title: Wujiang: The Land of Silk
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Wujiang District of Suzhou City on China’s east coast to explore the birthplace of silk. There we discover that silk is not merely a precious fabric but also a way of life.For centuries, Wujiang District has been one of China’s largest‑scale silk‑producing regions, which has turned it into a major commercial hub. Local residents worship a distinctive deity‑the Silkworm Goddess. Per the traditional Chinese lunar calendar, the Lesser Fullness of Grain (Xiaoman) solar term coincides with the goddess’s birthday. Local folk opera troupes take turns staging performances on the stage by the main temple hall over several days to mark the occasion and pray for good...

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill.Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge...

With red tiles and green trees that make up the city's stunning scenery, our hosts embark on another foodie-journey with local delicacies and interesting guest appearances. From drinking beer with a German friend, catching crabs by the ocean and devouring grilled eel the classic Korean way, this episode will leave you hungry for more!

programme.title: Life as a Miao Embroidery Girl
programme.desc: In this episode, host Eva May travels to Maomaohe Village in Leishan County, Guizhou Province — a place renowned for its exquisite Miao embroidery. She spends a week immersing herself in the daily lives of local embroidery artisans, learning traditional Miao folk songs, and rising to the challenge of creating a piece of Miaoxiu embroidery with special cultural significance.

programme.title: Wujiang: The Land of Silk
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Wujiang District of Suzhou City on China’s east coast to explore the birthplace of silk. There we discover that silk is not merely a precious fabric but also a way of life.For centuries, Wujiang District has been one of China’s largest‑scale silk‑producing regions, which has turned it into a major commercial hub. Local residents worship a distinctive deity‑the Silkworm Goddess. Per the traditional Chinese lunar calendar, the Lesser Fullness of Grain (Xiaoman) solar term coincides with the goddess’s birthday. Local folk opera troupes take turns staging performances on the stage by the main temple hall over several days to mark the occasion and pray for good...

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Five Ancestors Fist
programme.desc: In Quanzhou, southeast China, Kleber seeks out masters of the Five Ancestors Fist, a combination of five local kungfu styles. He meets the abbot of a Southern Shaolin Temple, and takes part in the extraordinary training regime used by Shaolin monks to hone their bodies and minds. He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill.Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge...

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-4 Medieval Combat
programme.desc: Episode 4 centres on Shanghai, where Eastern and Western martial traditions meet in surprising ways. Kleber visits local practitioners of Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA), trying German and Italian longsword techniques first-hand and seeing how Chinese enthusiasts innovate by combining European swordsmanship with ancient Chinese military manuals.The episode also follows the rise of BUHURT, a European-style armored combat sport now gaining traction in China, featuring locally made traditional Chinese armour in intense full-contact bouts. Through Kleber’s own multicultural martial arts studio and the city’s everyday East-West blend, the episode shows Shanghai as a global hub, a...

programme.title: The Elegance of Luoyang
programme.desc: Luoyang, as the eastern starting point of the Silk Road, is a city with a rich history and a tradition of cultural inclusivity. As such, it enjoys a prominent position in the heritage of the whole world.In this episode, we’ll visit White Horse Temple to learn about its fascinating international background. At Longmen Grottoes, which were designated as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in the year 2000, we’ll appreciate how the unique ancient splendor is being revived by 3D technology. At the city’s annual Peony Festival, we’ll explore the significance of China’s national flower and national dress.Invited to a Luoyang Water Banquet, we’ll learn something about the city’s culinary traditions....

programme.title: China Bound: Wuhan
programme.desc: Tianran He visits Wuhan, a megacity at the crossroads of central China. From experiencing its vibrant breakfast culture and iconic dishes like hot dry noodles to exploring the lakes and hills of the expansive East Lake, as well as historic districts that showcase a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, Tianran uncovers why Wuhan has been a pivotal city in Chinese history for centuries. Finally, he relives some of these moments through immersive theater performances set amongst historic buildings and aboard a steamship cruising the Yangtze River.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.4
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He travels to Shannan, the cradle of Tibetan culture. Nestled in the gentlest valley of the Yarlung Zangbo River, this is where the first Tibetan king rose to power, the first palace in Xizang was built, and many other “firsts” in Xizang’s history began. Tianran visits Yamdrok Lake, one of Xizang’s three sacred lakes, where a paragliding base is taking shape. He then learns the art of Tibetan opera, joins rangers on a mission to track the elusive Tibetan red deer, and ends the day with a rejuvenating soak in a village revitalized by hot spring tourism.

He experiences the intricacies of Quanzhou’s traditional puppetry, and learns how Five Ancestors Fist incorporated military tactics that allowed its practitioners to band together and fight off pirates.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-2 Chinese Wrestling
programme.desc: In Episode 2, Chinese Wrestling, host Kleber joins a public training session led by Wang Tongqing, a master preserving the imperial Shanpu Ying wrestling tradition. Swept up in the group’s lively atmosphere, he gets a first-hand feel for the master’s skill.Kleber then invites his Italian friend Paolo to train systematically, uncovering how Chinese wrestling principles connect with other martial arts, from Tai Chi to Wing Chun. Through Master Wang’s story of bringing a formerly imperial martial art into the public sphere, mentoring the next generation, and hoping to take it onto the international stage, the episode shows wrestling as more than a test of strength. It is a cultural bridge...

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan

programme.title: World Heritage in China: Ancient City of Pingyao
programme.desc: Established in the 14th century, Pingyao retains the typical layout of the county-level cities of the Han people in Central China. The ancient city is a complete community comprising walls, streets and lanes, shops, houses and temples.?As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Pingyao remains a testament to traditional Chinese urban planning and architecture, attracting visitors from around the world who seek to explore its historical streets and vibrant history.

programme.title: China Bound: Harbin
programme.desc: Tianran He is in Harbin, the "Ice City", host of the 2025 Asian Winter Games. Internationally renowned for its breathtaking ice and snow sculptures, the city thrives with activity despite it -20°C winters. From savoring the famous local ice cream and hearty northeastern Chinese dishes such as stewed goose and sweet-and-sour pork, to drifting on the frozen Songhua River and carving down the slopse of Yabuli Ski Resort, discover how much fun you can have in Harbin.

programme.title: China Untapped: Xizang Ep.5
programme.desc: In this final episode, Tianran journeys to Nyingchi, known as “Xizang’s Garden.” Here, he experiences the region’s semi-pastoral way of life — feeding yaks, trying his hand at archery, and seeing how tourism is transforming lives in Lulang International Tourist Town. Travelling along National Highway 318, Tianran discovers towering millennia-old cypress trees and rafts through the vast Yani National Wetland Park, before ending the day with a unique spa treatment at a traditional Tibetan hospital.

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuzhen
programme.desc: Join our hosts Tianran He and Eva May as they explore the boisterous event of Wuzhen's International Theatre festival, with colorful features of both theatrical and culinary nature. Foodie Tianran and art-lover Eva are accompanied by ubiquitous local street food, daily carnival performances and meet and greets with fascinating personalities. Let's set the stage for the beautiful merge of food and drama as they taste their way through the charming scene of Wuzhen.

programme.title: Foodwise：Eating Global in Beijing
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May are in search of global cuisines that can be found in Beijing, the 3000-year old capital of China. From honest farm-to-table fare, to the culinary heights of French haute cuisine, and even a cooking class and wine and dine event at a traditional courtyard home in the city center, we'll discover that in Beijing, you can taste the world.

programme.title: Life as a Miao Silversmith
programme.desc: In this episode, Eva May steps into Maliao Village — a century-old silversmith village nestled in Leishan, Guizhou Province. Over the course of a week, she dives into the craft and daily lives of Miao men who carry on the silversmithing legacy. She works side by side with local silversmiths day in and day out, delving into the culture and techniques behind Miao silverware. She even joins master silversmiths for a live-stream event, before engaging in discussions with university professors about how traditional craftsmanship can fuel rural revitalization. On top of that, she witnesses the breathtaking sight of "maidens adorned in silver and flowers" at the grand Miao New Year celebrations,...

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: White Crane
programme.desc: In Yongchun, China, Kleber explores the origins of White Crane kungfu and its effect on the martial arts world. He learns how its blocks and strikes were inspired by animal movements, and how acupuncture points can be used to deadly effect. After training his grip and finger strength with wooden sticks, he travels to Beijing for an introduction to Goju-ryu karate, and discovers striking similarities with White Crane.

programme.title: Meet China Episode 4
programme.desc: In this episode, we explore the cutting edge of Chinese industry. We visit China’s first offshore spaceport to see rockets launch toward the stars and move to Hangzhou’s E-Fashion Town, where AI turns designs into reality in seconds. We also follow the "fantastic journey" of a bag of garbage as it transforms into energy and bricks with the help of industrial intelligence. Finally, we explore the "emotional economy," where young people find solace in trendy toys and historical fragrances.

programme.title: Why China's theme parks are having a moment
programme.desc: Looking for a cool summer escape with a twist? China’s theme parks are more than rides—they’re immersive worlds of blockbuster stories, spectacular shows, high-tech thrills, and local flavors.Earlier this year, CGTN's Lincoln Humphries and Yu Hongyu explored two of China's best-known parks to see why they’re drawing crowds from across the country. From unforgettable live performances to next-level interactive experiences, discover a fresh way to travel in China.

programme.title: Europe's heating up: So where is the AC?
programme.desc: CGTN reporter Li Jianhua reports on how Londoners live without air conditioning, despite the British summers getting longer and heater.

programme.title: So many UK Prime Ministers, same old problems
programme.desc: Since moving to London, CGTN's Li Jianhua has witnessed the UK cycle through four leaders. In this video, Jianhua reflects on the problems facing each of those prime ministers… and why it's affected how he buys grapes.

programme.title: Who owns Britain?
programme.desc: One of the first things that surprised CGTN's Li Jianhua after moving to Britain was discovering that London’s iconic black cabs are made by a subsidiary of China’s Geely. It’s not alone. Jaguar Land Rover belongs to India’s Tata, Mini is owned by Germany’s BMW, and many of Britain’s airports, utilities and landmark buildings have foreign owners. For decades, Britain embraced global investment. But the battle over British Steel suggests attitudes are changing. As concerns grow around national security and economic resilience, the question is no longer just who invests in Britain — but which industries are too strategic to be foreign-owned. In this latest episode of his series...

programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode...

programme.title: China's rural CEO experiment: How a Dai village is reinventing itself
programme.desc: During the Dai New Year, CGTN reporter Lincoln Humphries visited Manluanzhan, a traditional Dai village near China's southwestern border in Yunnan Province. There, "sleeping" assets are being awakened: an abandoned water tower has been turned into a café, and traditional Dai houses have been expanded to offer new types of homestays.At the center of this experiment is an unusual figure — a rural CEO who helps balance economic development with the Dai community's traditions as the village charts its own path forward.In this episode of #BizFocus, Lincoln Humphries shows how a village in Xishuangbanna brings fresh vitality and authentic traditions together.

programme.title: The new keeper of the ancient village in the deep mountains
programme.desc: Deep in the mountains of Fujian, Yanxiang village is home to centuries-old Hakka architecture and an aging population. But a post 1995-born returnee is giving the ancient village a new future.Follow CGTN’s He Jingyi to see how a young village chief blends modern ideas with traditional heritage, breathing new life into this millennium-old rural settlement. #BizFocus

programme.title: How rafting helped one village find new life
programme.desc: In Sankengtan Village, Guangdong Province, a river that once flowed quietly through everyday life is now part of the Gulong Gorge rafting course—a global destination drawing millions of visitors each year. What was once a quiet rural community has been transformed by tourism, as local residents build new livelihoods around the river and the opportunities it brings. In this episode of BizFocus, CGTN's Vivienne Nunis joins those braving the white water to find out more.

programme.title: Policy push brings smart homes into everyday life
programme.desc: China has expanded and upgraded its dual-new policy package, marking the first-ever inclusion of smart home products in central government consumption subsidies. CGTN reporter He Jingyi explores the Beijing Premium Housing Tech Expo, testing out smart home systems with voice control and automatic sensory adjustment. She also visits offline Suning stores, speaking with outlet managers and customers to uncover how smart home solutions are gaining mainstream traction, entering ordinary households, and driving the upgrade of China’s manufacturing industry.

programme.title: Behind CXMT IPO and China’s chip roadmap
programme.desc: As CXMT makes its market debut on Shanghai's STAR Market, the listing is drawing attention far beyond the trading floor. As China's top DRAM producer, CXMT sits at the center of the country's push to strengthen its semiconductor capabilities and build a more resilient technology ecosystem. What does the IPO mean for investors, the capital market, and the future of the global memory-chip industry? Join us on BizTalk as we explore market forces, policy priorities and the roadmap to technology self-reliance behind the landmark listing.

programme.title: China's rural CEO experiment: How a Dai village is reinventing itself
programme.desc: During the Dai New Year, CGTN reporter Lincoln Humphries visited Manluanzhan, a traditional Dai village near China's southwestern border in Yunnan Province. There, "sleeping" assets are being awakened: an abandoned water tower has been turned into a café, and traditional Dai houses have been expanded to offer new types of homestays.At the center of this experiment is an unusual figure — a rural CEO who helps balance economic development with the Dai community's traditions as the village charts its own path forward.In this episode of #BizFocus, Lincoln Humphries shows how a village in Xishuangbanna brings fresh vitality and authentic traditions together.

programme.title: How rafting helped one village find new life
programme.desc: In Sankengtan Village, Guangdong Province, a river that once flowed quietly through everyday life is now part of the Gulong Gorge rafting course—a global destination drawing millions of visitors each year. What was once a quiet rural community has been transformed by tourism, as local residents build new livelihoods around the river and the opportunities it brings. In this episode of BizFocus, CGTN's Vivienne Nunis joins those braving the white water to find out more.

Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode...

programme.title: China's rural CEO experiment: How a Dai village is reinventing itself
programme.desc: During the Dai New Year, CGTN reporter Lincoln Humphries visited Manluanzhan, a traditional Dai village near China's southwestern border in Yunnan Province. There, "sleeping" assets are being awakened: an abandoned water tower has been turned into a café, and traditional Dai houses have been expanded to offer new types of homestays.At the center of this experiment is an unusual figure — a rural CEO who helps balance economic development with the Dai community's traditions as the village charts its own path forward.In this episode of #BizFocus, Lincoln Humphries shows how a village in Xishuangbanna brings fresh vitality and authentic traditions together.

programme.title: The new keeper of the ancient village in the deep mountains
programme.desc: Deep in the mountains of Fujian, Yanxiang village is home to centuries-old Hakka architecture and an aging population. But a post 1995-born returnee is giving the ancient village a new future.Follow CGTN’s He Jingyi to see how a young village chief blends modern ideas with traditional heritage, breathing new life into this millennium-old rural settlement. #BizFocus

programme.title: How rafting helped one village find new life
programme.desc: In Sankengtan Village, Guangdong Province, a river that once flowed quietly through everyday life is now part of the Gulong Gorge rafting course—a global destination drawing millions of visitors each year. What was once a quiet rural community has been transformed by tourism, as local residents build new livelihoods around the river and the opportunities it brings. In this episode of BizFocus, CGTN's Vivienne Nunis joins those braving the white water to find out more.

programme.title: Policy push brings smart homes into everyday life
programme.desc: China has expanded and upgraded its dual-new policy package, marking the first-ever inclusion of smart home products in central government consumption subsidies. CGTN reporter He Jingyi explores the Beijing Premium Housing Tech Expo, testing out smart home systems with voice control and automatic sensory adjustment. She also visits offline Suning stores, speaking with outlet managers and customers to uncover how smart home solutions are gaining mainstream traction, entering ordinary households, and driving the upgrade of China’s manufacturing industry.

programme.title: Behind CXMT IPO and China’s chip roadmap
programme.desc: As CXMT makes its market debut on Shanghai's STAR Market, the listing is drawing attention far beyond the trading floor. As China's top DRAM producer, CXMT sits at the center of the country's push to strengthen its semiconductor capabilities and build a more resilient technology ecosystem. What does the IPO mean for investors, the capital market, and the future of the global memory-chip industry? Join us on BizTalk as we explore market forces, policy priorities and the roadmap to technology self-reliance behind the landmark listing.

programme.title: Meet China: When Chinese Dynamism Reshapes Landscapes — Boundless Challenges, Infinite Vitality
programme.desc: In this episode of Meet China, we journey from the cloud-piercing peaks of Zhangjiajie to the tech-driven streets of Shenzhen and the cassava farms of Vietnam. We meet extreme athletes redefining personal limits, turning vertical cliffs and open skies into new playgrounds. Then, we ride in a fully autonomous robotaxi through Shenzhen traffic, exploring the technology and regulations accelerating the global race for self-driving cars. Finally, we travel to Vietnam, where Chinese investment and expertise have transformed the cassava industry—boosting yields, stabilizing farmer incomes, and creating resilient supply chains reaching global markets. From skies to roads to fields, this episode...

programme.desc: Firefighters in Barbizieux, Charente are called to a fire at a large house in the village; they arrive to find the lifeless body of the owner, 83-year-old Claude Tavernier, lying in a large pool of blood.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Police in Strasbourg receive a startling emergency call from Doctor Jean-Louis Muller, a forensic pathologist well known in the region.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: 18-year-old Laetitia Perrais is a trainee hotel waitress who vanishes after an evening shift; every attempt is made to shed light on her disappearance and the efforts eventually pay off.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Shot In the While Sleeping (Richard Alessandri Case): On the night of July 16, 2000, the life of Edwige Alessandri changed forever. This mother, married to a supermarket boss, made a frantic emergency call in the town of Carpentras. She recounted that shortly after midnight, some men burst into her room and shot her husband while he slept. Who could have despised Richard Alessandri enough to kill him in cold blood in his own bed? Was he the victim of a robbery gone wrong, as claimed by his wife?

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: A Dire Deception (LAURENCE MAILLE CASE): On November 28, 2007, Laurence Maille disappeared. It was her partner, John Zablevski, who alerted the Vimy police in Pas-de-Calais. He explained that the young woman had left in the morning for a walk with their dog and never returned. An unprecedented search was immediately launched to try to find her. Beautiful, intelligent and generous, Laurence Maille had everything to be happy about and for 18 months, had found the perfect love in her partner.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: The Mystery of Room 602 (Véronique Pirotton Case): On October 31, 2013, Belgian politician Bernard Ouessfal rushed down the six flights of a hotel in Ostend where he had met up with his wife, Véronique, the day before. He had just found her unconscious on the bathroom floor with a mysterious plastic bag next to her. Despite the emergency rescue response, Véronique Pirotton died a few minutes later.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Two Accused of Murder (Jennifer Charron Case) - On Sunday, April 29, 2007, the body of Jennifer Charron, 21-years old, was found burnt to a crisp in a forest near Royan. The young waitress, who had been missing for two days, was visibly beaten and tied up. In this astonishing case, the clues examined by the experts will give them two leads: two men, two suspects with very different profiles... but investigators are convinced that they both have a direct link with the murder.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: THE CASE OF STÉPHANE KAMEUGNE - On December 24, 2008, the body of Stéphane Kameugne was fished out from a canal in Châlons-en-Champagne. The young man had been missing for two weeks and no one had seen him since the evening of his graduation ceremony from his engineering school. A theory soon emerged: the very drunk student had fallen over thea bridge over the canal which led to his death. But his parents and relatives did not believe this.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: The Savage Murder of a Mother and her Daughter (Amato Case)- On March 31, 2003, firefighters were called to a fire in a housing estate of Meyrargues, near Aix-en-Provence. On site, they discovered a horrific scene: the tortured and charred bodies of a mother and her daughter, Chantal and Audrey D'Amato, aged 53 and 24 respectively.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: A Night of Horror at Devil's Plateau (Marie-Jeanne Meyer Case) - On June 18, 2011, Marie-Jeanne Meyer, 17-years old, waved goodbye to her little sister before leaving for her daily jog on the heights of Tournon in Ardèche. She never came back. Three days later, her mutilated body was found in a freshly dug pit, near an area known to be cursed, "The Devil's Plateau." What's more, the crime scene looked like a mystical ritual ... Was it a ritual murder? Revenge? An unfortunate encounter? ...

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: A Mysterious Murder at the Farm (Valérie Bary Case)- On Friday, March 26, 2004, in the region of Dijon, Laurent Bary came home from his work to discover the lifeless body of his wife, Valerie, bathing in a pool of blood. According to the investigators' initial findings, the 38-year-old nurse's aid had been stabbed several times, seeming to validate the theory of a robbery gone wrong.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: On July 13, 2011, two boaters retrieved a suitcase that was floating in the bay of Lorient. Inside, they discovered the tied up corpse of a man.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Bloody Christmas next to the Leman lake (CASE OF RUTH LÉGERET) - On January 4, 2006, Ruth Légeret was found dead in the middle of a pool of blood at her luxurious property in Vevey, Switzerland. Next to her was the lifeless body of her friend, Marina Studer. Who could have killed these two simple and wealthy widows? Clue after clue, the Swiss police's investigation would revolve around an environment of family jealousy and financial greed.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: September 16 2005. The lifeless body of Audrey Jouannet, 24, is found hidden under the bed in her small apartment in Soisy-sur-Seine. It soon becomes apparent that the young woman has been tortured at length before being strangled. But surprisingly, though the highly meticulous murderer has taken care to leave no sign of his passage, the autopsy reveals traces of sperm on the victim. It will take all of the investigators' intuition to pierce the mystery of this heinous crime...

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Sylvain Dromard finds the body of his wife Laurence lying in a pool of blood in the kitchen. The crime was particularly violent and the theory of a burglary that went wrong is soon excluded. But investigators don't understand who could want the adorable hairdresser of Saint-Martin-d'Ablois dead. During the investigation, the work of profilers will enable them to draw a very precise portrait of the murderer...

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: After an ordinary dinner, Pierre and Gabrielle Labrell suffer severe abdominal pains.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Nelly Crémel, 39, leaves her home to go jogging... never to return. Eight days later, after a vast search campaign, her body is found. There's no doubt that it's murder. The case soon ignites public opinion, even inflaming passions at the highest level of the state. The clues lead investigators on a number of trails, from the shadows of the French secret service to a manhunt for a possible sex maniac, in a case of murder most foul.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Willy Pomonti, a retired architect, is found savagely murdered in his opulent villa in La Celle-Saint-Cloud, near Paris.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: The lifeless body of Christophe Lejard is found by his son just metres from their home.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: A man walks into a gendarmerie near Saint-Malo to report that his wife has been missing since the previous day. The couple are going through a divorce, but this mother would never have left her seven children alone! An extensive search is undertaken but the woman cannot be found. What has happened to Adeline Piet? The investigation spans several years and experiences many twists.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: The corpse of Priscillia Ciatti, 14, is discovered by the side of a field, a few hundred metres from her family home. The teenager has been stabbed sixty times with a knife and -an extra sordid detail - a devil mask is found next to her body. Was Priscillia the victim of a prowler? A serial killer? A maniac inspired by a horror movie? Investigators soon find that the young girl felt she was being watched, and even threatened...

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: In the early hours of the morning, Mathilde Croguennec, 18, attending "Teknival" in Brittany, is found at the foot of a tree with her throat cut. Investigators face the task of finding the killer from among the 43,000 participants of this huge open-air festival of electronic music, where drink and drugs are consumed in abundance. An unusual investigation that leads the police down a number of false avenues.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: Arriving at her work, the secretary of a small firm in the suburbs of Geneva finds the body of Jean-Raymond Blatti, the company's new accountant. The man is lying in a pool of blood and, on his belly, the murderer has written "DIRTY RAPIST". Yet Jean-Raymond Blatti was never charged with sexual assault. Over the course of the investigation, this inscription will appear as one of the many mysteries of this case which is particularly rich in twists and turns.

programme.title: Crime Scene Solvers
programme.desc: On July 19th 2004, the naked and tied up body of a woman is recovered in the Ourcq canal in Fresnes-sur-Marne. The victim is impossible to identify.

programme.title: Raider Of The Lost Art
programme.desc: When Van Gogh died, he was a complete unknown, his paintings fetching under 10 dollars. So how did his works become some of the most revered and expensive in the world? His sister-in-law Johanna is to thank for that. With a new Van Gogh having been discovered just last year, where are the rest?

programme.title: Raider Of The Lost Art
programme.desc: During WWII the Nazis plundered some of the world's greatest artworks as they tore across Europe. We find out how the Allies tracked them down, what they saved, and what is still missing to this day.

programme.title: Raider Of The Lost Art
programme.desc: The story of the theft of the Mona Lisa in 1911 from the Louvre and how Pablo Picasso was accused of the crime. Plus, the incredible tales of how many other of da Vinci's works were lost to history and had to be reclaimed.

programme.title: Raider Of The Lost Art
programme.desc: The Dutch didn't appreciate what they had. For 200 years Vermeer was completely forgotten. Trying to recover a lost man's masterpieces has driven men to great extremes and gave rise to one of the greatest forgers the world has ever seen.

programme.title: Raider Of The Lost Art
programme.desc: In Munich, in 2013 a giant haul of missing masterpieces was discovered. Cornelius Gurlitt was the man behind it and we investigate how his father's job was to purchase works for Hitler himself as part of his Fuhrermuseum.

programme.title: Raider Of The Lost Art
programme.desc: Each year Carl Fabergé made one of a kind Easter egg for the Tsar's family. But Carl was forced to flee Russia during the revolution and 8 of these priceless Imperial Eggs went missing. With one of the elusive 8 recently uncovered could the other seven have survived the chaos of 1917?

programme.title: Bronze Age
programme.sub-title: S01 : E01 Part 1: Rise of Civilization
programme.desc: In the region that includes the Mediterranean, the Aegean, Mesopotamia and Egypt, the Bronze Age arrived about 3000 BC and lasted nearly 2000 years. What singled out this period and the new societies and cities that emerged? The development of formal writing is one among several important factors.

programme.title: Bronze Age
programme.sub-title: S01 : E02 Part 2: Masters Of Trade
programme.desc: Trade, and in particular trade in luxury goods, drove the commerce economies of the Bronze Age. This is the time when the first super powers in history, Egypt and Mesopotamia, emerge and dominate the "world" stage of the Mediterranean and Aegean seas and surrounding areas.

programme.title: Bronze Age
programme.sub-title: S01 : E03 Part 3: Conquest And Collapse
programme.desc: The Bronze Age had the first large urban centers, powerful kingdoms and armies, writing, and trade routes across vast areas. What led to the collapse of the city-state entities and the end of the Bronze Age? Possibly a perfect storm of uncontrollable factors that are still being researched.

programme.title: Deep Time History
programme.sub-title: S01 : E01 Episode 1: The Rise Of Civilization
programme.desc: About 8,000 BC, in a few select places some people begin to experiment with a new way of harvesting energy. They’re growing their own crops.

programme.title: Deep Time History
programme.sub-title: S01 : E02 Episode 2: The Age Of Discovery
programme.desc: Columbus has no idea that because of Earth’s geology and geography he won't get to his destination…or how that failure made his voyage one of the most influential.

programme.title: Deep Time History
programme.sub-title: S01 : E03 Episode 3: The Industrial Revolution And Modern Warfare
programme.desc: How do prehistoric forests link to the development of steam engines, and the rise of modern industry?

programme.title: Breakthrough
programme.desc: New evidence suggests humans arrived in North America far earlier than previously thought, and that they may have traveled along paths now buried deep beneath the sea.

programme.title: Breakthrough
programme.sub-title: S01 : E07 Herculaneum Scrolls: Unraveling History
programme.desc: The eruption of Mount Vesuvius is renowned for its decimation of Pompeii, but nearby, an equally impressive Roman settlement known as Herculaneum was lost to history.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: S01 : E01 The Vikings: Origin of the Vikings
programme.desc: From the ice fields of the North to the Russian steppe, these fearsome Scandinavian warriors sailed the globe for three centuries spreading their net of trade and pillage

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: S01 : E02 The Vikings: Early Viking Society and Religion
programme.desc: In this episode, we learn how early Viking society developed, what the sacred rituals really were, and what role women played in Viking religion.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: S01 : E03 The Vikings: The Ships of the Vikings
programme.desc: Ships carried Nordic warriors all the way from their Scandinavian homes to lands of conquest. How were these ergonomic ships built and what made them so special?

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: S01 : E04 The Vikings: Weapons of the Vikings
programme.desc: The Vikings were fighting machines, plundering lands from central Asia to North America and defeated the armies of the greatest empires. What was their secret?

programme.desc: A bank vault was blasted into from the ceiling, and over $2 million in valuables was missing. Agents were able to track down one of the robbers' friends and attempted to use him as bait to reel in the crooks.

programme.title: The FBI Files

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: In February 1988, a record store clerk in Ohio was fatally shot in his van. After discovering thousands of dollars in the vehicle, police knew that robbery was not the motive.

programme.desc: A sniper murdered two Black men as they jogged with two white women. The FBI placed their suspect on their Ten Most Wanted list and began an intense manhunt. What followed was the arrest, trial and conviction of a white supremacist serial killer.

programme.title: The FBI Files
programme.desc: After a parole officer was found shot dead in his car, the FBI, DEA and NYPD struggled to contain the mounting violence from drug gangs that continued to escalate. Authorities sought to put two ruthless drug kingpins behind bars for the crime.

programme.desc: In October 1987, a Boston police officer responding to a domestic disturbance call was fatally wounded.

programme.desc: An escapee from Castro's Cuba was the mastermind behind a secret terrorist organization called Omega 7.

programme.title: GLORY Kickboxing
programme.sub-title: S00 : E01 GLORY 105: Last Heavyweight Standing Finals
programme.desc: In the quarter finals, Belgian Moroccan Anis Bouzid (48-4, 37 KO) takes on kickboxing legend Errol Zimmerman (112-20-1, 45 KO), Serbian sensation Milos Cvjeticanin (17-5, 10 KO) meets number one French heavyweight Sofian Laidouni (42-5-1, 20 KO), monstrous Tariq ‘Cookie’ Osaro (29-4-1, 16 KO) clashes with ‘The Soldier’ Nidal Bchiri (20-5-1, 5 KO), and ‘The Black Ghost’ Mory Kromah (35-3-1, 21 KO) collides with outspoken rival Michael ‘Timebomb’ Boapeah (23-5-1, 29 KO). Only one fighter can come out on top and walk away as the new ‘King of Kickboxing’. Elsewhere, the always exciting Bahram Rajabzadeh (72-6, 64 KO) goes up against ‘The Gladiator’ Cristian Ristea (44-27, 13 KO), Hamicha (42-2, 31 KO) puts his undefeated GLORY record on the line against late replacement Brice Kombou (20-6, 5 KO), and featherweights Andre Santos (23-2, 10 KO) and Deniz Demirkapu (15-5, 10 KO) will kick-off the main card.

programme.title: GLORY Kickboxing
programme.desc: GLORY 103: Last Heavyweight Standing main event features Levi Rigters (19-3, 9 KO) colliding with Jamal Ben Saddik (38-10, 29 KO) to see who moves on in the tournament. Among the other names taking part in Phase Two are Nabil Khachab (29-6-1, 4 KO), Iancu Ionut (31-11, 13 KO), Rade Opacic (21-7, 16 KO), Milos Cvjeticanin (13-4, 9 KO), Sofian Laidouni (39-5-1, 20 KO), and many more. In addition, Chico Kwasi (44-5-2, 23 KO) will defend his GLORY welterweight world title against Mehdi Ait El Hadj (35-4-2, 8 KO), Mory Kromah (34-3-1, 20 KO) returns and takes on Cristian Ristea (44-26, 13 KO) in a heavyweight match-up outside the tournament, and Tayfun Ozcan (88-11-3, 28 KO) clashes with rival Don Sno (6-2, 3 KO).

programme.title: GLORY Kickboxing
programme.desc: Former Light Heavyweight Champion Tarik Khbabez (52-12-1, 22 KO) and Bahram Rajabzabeh (72-5, 63 KO) collide in a huge showdown for the vacant Light Heavyweight title. The penultimate round of the Last Heavyweight Standing tournament resumes with eight heavyweights competing in two separate four-man one-night tournaments. Notable participants include Levi Rigters (20-3, 10 KO), Nabil Khachab (30-6-1, 4 KO), Rade Opacic (22-7, 17 KO) and Milos Cvjeticanin (14-4, 9 KO).

programme.title: GLORY Kickboxing
programme.desc: Over the course of a year, twelve of the best GLORY featherweights will compete opposite twelve of the best RISE featherweights in a series of knockout bouts until one fighter becomes the Last Featherweight Standing.

programme.title: GLORY Kickboxing
programme.sub-title: S00 : E07 GLORY 102 Featherweight Grand Prix
programme.desc: Four more will punch their tickets into the next round as GLORY & RISE search for the baddest featherweight on the planet in this year long tournament. On the GLORY side, top ranked German Polish fighter Denis Wosik (40-9-1, 9 KO) takes on Thai veteran Suarek (107-40-11, 39 KO) and Italy’s Achraf Aasila (53-13, 13 KO) meets France’s Lounis Saing (19-4-1, 12 KO). Meanwhile on the RISE side of the bracket, Japan’s Yutaro Asahi (17-9, 4 KO) clashes with Spain’s Eduardo Catalin (17-3-1) and top Japanese prospect Yura Kono (15-1, 7 KO) goes up against China’s Dexiang Kong (35-10). In addition to the Last Featherweight Standing matchups, Shiro Matsumoto (53-17-4, 18 KO) defends his RISE bantamweight title against top challenger Masahi Kumura (24-7, 12 KO) and Australian KO artists Chadd Collins (64-18-2, 32) defends his RISE super lightweight championship against the great Kento Haraguchi (25-4-1, 14 KO).

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: This week in the Welsh heat newcomer Andrew Birch is challenging two returning chefs, Adam Bannister and Phil Carmichael. It is the dessert course and one chef will go home.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Today is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from Wales are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, blogger and food writer Rosie Birkett.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Three newcomers are competing to become regional Central champion - Daniel Smith, Andrew Scott and Danny Gill. Danny Gill is a former head chef at Daniel Cliffords two star restaurant Midsummer House.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and the chefs are using some of the UKs best seafood: lobster, salmon and Cornish crab. Daniel Smith may be classically trained but hes decided to take a risk adding a cheese custard to his lobster dish.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Two chefs are cooking venison. Danny Gill is making a venison wellington, inspired by his Dad, a former RAF chef who has served up Wellington for royalty. While Andrew Scott has sourced his venison from the Queens Scottish estate, Balmoral.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: This week three chefs from the central region are fighting to be crowned champion. Today one competitor will go home, only the two highest scoring chefs will make it through to the judging chamber. And the chefs are pushing themselves.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Today is the head to head. The Central regions two highest scoring chefs are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort, for the very first time.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.sub-title: S11 : E26 London and South East Starter
programme.desc: Today three of the most exciting talents from London and the South East region are competing for a place in the National Finals.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.sub-title: S11 : E27 London and South East Fish
programme.desc: It is the fish course and chef Russell Bateman is celebrating the diversity of his beloved home town of London by combining lobster with jerk spices for an ambitious fish course with seven key elements.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.sub-title: S11 : E28 London and South East Main
programme.desc: Its the all important main course and returning contender Mark Froydenlund is banking on it being his strongest dish. Hes showcasing British Rose veal and celebrating the determination of British producers to bounce back from disaster.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.sub-title: S11 : E29 London and South East Dessert
programme.desc: Its the dessert course and the final chance for three of London and South Easts most competitive and talented chefs to get through to the judging chamber, today the veteran judge will send one chef home.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.sub-title: S11 : E30 London and South East Judging
programme.desc: Today is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from the London and South East region are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort. Joining this week as Guest judge is Kevin Gould, an award winning food writer.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Mini Patel is back for a second attempt at the North East Regional title but hes competing against two young newcomers Tommy Banks and Chris Archer.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the fish course and two chefs from the North East, Tommy and Mini, have very similar ingredients - both are cooking mackerel.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Its the main course of the North East Region and overnight there has been a dramatic development. Its a tough and emotional day for the chefs.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is a highly emotional day for one of the chefs as he prepares a dish which is inspired by and a tribute to his own Great Briton, his late Grandfather.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Today the two chefs are cooking for the judges Matthew Fort, Prue Leith and Oliver Peyton. Joining them is guest judge is John Williams MBE, the executive Head Chef at The Ritz, the only hotel to hold a royal warrant for banqueting.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: This week three top chefs from Northern Ireland are competing for a place in the National Finals. There are some varied and exciting starters, as the chefs get creative. And theres real shock and emotion as the veteran chef delivers his scores.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Today the atmosphere in the kitchen gets even more competitive as the three chefs from Northern Ireland dish cook their fish courses.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the main course and returning Chef Chris McGowan is feeling confident but part of his dish involves making his own venison sausages to serve with a venison rack, and getting it all done in time is straining his emotions.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: The three chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking their desserts and one chef is on course for an historic score, he could beat his boss a veteran of GBM and achieve more marks than anyone has done throughout the history of the competition.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Today is the head to head. The two highest scoring chefs from Northern Ireland are cooking for judges Oliver Peyton, Prue Leith and Matthew Fort who are joined by guest judge, restaurant critic and Editor-at-Large of the Independent, Amol Rajan.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It's the National Finals of Great British Menu. The chefs will mark each course of the fellow chefs dishes; the average of their scores will be added to the judges scores. There are some shocks and surprises as the chefs opinions differ from the judges.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is day two of Great British Menus National Finals. Today the eight champions will cook their fish courses. Two chefs have reason to be confident after scoring tens from every judge in the heats. Can they deliver a perfect dish second time round?

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the National Finals of Great British Menu and main course day, the one course every chef wants to cook at the banquet. It is a nerve wracking day for three of the eight regional champions.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: It is the final day of the competition in this years Great British Menu, this is the last chance for the eight champions to get one of their dishes to the banquet for Queen Elizabeth lls Great Britons.

programme.title: Great British Menu
programme.desc: Great British Menus winning chefs arrive at the Palace of Westminster to cook for the Banquet of Great Britons. As the banquet is served the chefs show just why they are amongst the best in the country.

programme.desc: Two outlaws posing as Cisco and Pancho are wreaking havoc. When the real Cisco and Pancho are captured, the criminals plan a final heist, using the duo as alibis. After breaking them out of jail, the real heroes have a chance to escape and clear their names by capturing the imposters. Will they succeed or be caught again?

programme.title: White Fang
programme.desc: The wolf dog, White Fang, aids a reporter, a fur trapper, a nun, a young Eskimo boy and his father of ridding a gold mining town of a sleazy crime lord in 1896 Yukon, Canada.

programme.title: Requiescant
programme.desc: The adopted son of a preacher comes upon a village that is under the thumb of a deranged ex-Confederate officer, who is - among other things - stealing land from the locals with phony land grants.

programme.title: My Gun is the Law
programme.desc: In San Felipe, bandits target gold meant for the railroad - until a decoy chest thwarts them. When newcomers arrive, a masked gunman begins sabotaging the outlaws. But the real mastermind may be the town’s respected leader, hiding treachery behind wealth and charm.

programme.title: 10,000 Dollars for a Massacre
programme.desc: 10,000 Dollars for a Massacre - Django has become a bounty hunter who is asked to chase a villain who has kidnapped a young girl.

programme.title: Seven Guns for the MacGregors
programme.desc: Ranch owner MacGregor has seven sons and oldest Gregor leads his brothers to Las Mesas, a small town where they want to sell horses. They get into trouble with local people who are related with evil Santillana. After getting imprisoned and losing their horses they decide to go after Santillana's gang.

programme.title: Molly And Lawless John
programme.desc: In New Mexico, a sheriff's unhappy mid-aged wife aids a condemned prisoner escape her husband's jail and elopes with the young and attractive outlaw to Mexico, pursued by the sheriff's posse.

programme.title: Showdown At Williams Creek
programme.desc: A British soldier decides to move to the American frontier and start a new life. He finds the frontier tough and struggles with the climate, thieves and swindlers. He is accused of murder and put on trial.

programme.title: Kill Django... Kill First
programme.desc: In a mining town, Johnny MaGee clashes with banker Anthony Burton, who uses bandits and deceit to seize gold mines and control the economy. Partnering with an old miner, Johnny seeks justice, while navigating love, betrayal, and alliances. As tensions rise, a bounty hunter joins the fray, promising a final showdown against corruption.

programme.title: The Shooting
programme.desc: A mysterious woman persuades two cowboys to help her in a revenge scheme.

programme.title: Quintana: Dead or Alive
programme.desc: In a Mexican province oppressed by the evil Governor Don Juan de Leyra, the rebel-outlaw Quintana is the sole guardian of justice.

programme.title: Djurado
programme.desc: Djurado is a gun-slinging professional gambler who struts into the small town of Silver Mine and wins half of the local saloon, the other part of which belongs to Barbara, whilst battling notorious outlaw Tucan.

programme.title: The Covered Wagon
programme.desc: Two wagon caravans converge at what is now Kansas City, and combine for the westward push to Oregon. On their quest the pilgrims will experience desert heat, mountain snow, hunger, and indian attack.

programme.title: And Now... Make Your Peace with God
programme.desc: Two men ride toward Denver City, each chasing a ghost from the past—one seeks his father’s killer, the other a treacherous friend who stole his gold. Along the way, a silent, deadly gunslinger joins them, his motives unknown. In the shadows of vengeance, alliances shift and secrets unravel.

programme.title: The Grand Duel
programme.desc: A grizzled ex-sheriff helps a man framed for murder to confront the powerful trio of brothers who want him dead.

programme.title: Guns Of The Revolution
programme.desc: In Mexico, a mad general is leading his own war against the Church.

programme.title: Dead Aim
programme.desc: A traveling gravedigger during an war adopts a orphan he finds alone in the desert. After the war with the orphan grown and business slow, the orphan begins to generate business himself by shooting people.

programme.title: Tepepa
programme.desc: In early 20th century Mexico, Tepepa, a revolutionary hero, is set to be executed by Cascorro’s men. Just as the firing squad prepares, Doctor Henry Price, an Englishman, arrives and saves Tepepa. However, Price’s true intentions are revealed when he coldly explains that he saved him only to have the pleasure of killing him himself.
